RagShortTexts: Brabançons and Routier companies offered lethal pike discipline but devastated countryside.

Variants.Content: Hardened free companies from Brabant and Flanders, known as Brabançons and routiers, sold their pikes and arbalests to European sovereigns. These bands had no lasting ties to any lord, and each company followed the contract that paid best. Their cohesion on the field made them dependable against cavalry charges, but in peacetime the lack of discipline and the absence of wages turned them into marauders. They raided villages, ransacked the grain stores of the countryside, and sometimes desecrated abbeys, which earned them excommunication from church councils. Their reputation followed them from one war to the next, and rulers who hired them had to pay for the damage they left behind.

Royal promises are wind, and silver marks in the belt pouch are the only certainty. A Brabant pike square marches shoulder to shoulder and holds its ground under cavalry. Withhold our wages and we will take payment from your grain barns, with fire if we must. Every captain counts the money before the drum sounds.
A plague of locusts is gentler than Brabançon hirelings. They take our seed corn, roast the village prior to extort altar chalices, and leave nothing behind but burnt thatch and weeping widows.
